source_support.contribution: Requires a functional baseline before efficiency changes.
Defines refactoring by preservation of externally visible behavior.
Distinguishes change intents while centering preservation of existing behavior.
Supplies a practical stop signal when consequential prerequisites cannot be responsibly defended.
Technical ability to make a change does not confer authority to select or authorize it; proposed changes should pass through explicit evaluation and approval before execution.
Refines authority discipline with a positive stop rule at the accepted target and escalation for wider tradeoffs.
Requires stating uncertainty, accepting responsibility, and declining or renegotiating unsupported commitments.
Recursive discovery swept subagent session files into a backfill scoped to top-level sessions; discovery pattern narrowed to exactly the intended population.
Photo preview's native-default activation and shifting geometry replaced with designed per-phase states: reserved geometry, explicit loading and error states, deliberate activation.

States that failure modes exist whether or not you design them - if you do not design your failure modes you get whatever unpredictable and usually dangerous ones happen to emerge - the designed-versus-incidental principle this concept applies to asynchronous UI states.
Unbounded packet dump into the consumer's context replaced by a bounded, ranked, size-budgeted brief rendered over unchanged canonical JSON.
Dangling job id and unknown enum value in hand-authored declarative config; cross-references validated against the authoritative set at load.

Prescribes verifying in advance that every referenced resource is present and failing immediately - the renderer checked for the presence of every font image background and mask before spending compute - rather than failing downstream after work is wasted.
Early exit before ranking silently substituted arrival order for relevance; fix scores the entire bounded candidate set before truncation and composes match text from content fields only.
Supports failing-test-first for repair while warning that feature-by-feature TDD can displace broader interface design.
Presents test-first as a feedback technique while retaining contextual validity for test-last.
Connects unit tests developed with code to contract and testability feedback.

Carries the paging-versus-diagnosis rule: black-box monitoring is symptom-oriented and for paging forces the discipline of nagging a human only for ongoing, real-symptom problems, while white-box instrumentation serves diagnosis and imminent-failure detection; also notes symptom and cause are layer-relative in multilayered systems.

States the two-question split verbatim - monitoring should address what is broken (the symptom) and why (the cause) - with the symptom-cause example table, and names the what-versus-why distinction as central to maximum-signal minimum-noise monitoring.

Enumerates latency, traffic, errors, and saturation, and defines errors beyond protocol codes - explicit failures, implicit wrong-content successes, and policy failures - noting load-balancer catches versus end-to-end tests for wrong content.
Documents the GitHub incident where reused primary keys conflated distinct records across MySQL and Redis, silently disclosing private data - the consequence of a key not pinning one logical record.

Shows that an identifier failing to name a particular version of a record conflates distinct records and makes results wrong; the fix is widening the identifier - the slowly-changing-dimension version key.

States the loud-abort uniqueness mechanism - INSERT under a UNIQUE constraint fails visibly on collision - which is the safe default this concept prefers over silent suppression, and derives the request identifier from all relevant fields.
UNIQUE key widened to include manifest_id and ON CONFLICT corrected; the dedup key now covers every dimension of the record's true logical identity.
Fabricated external model identifier corrected against the provider's real catalog; identifiers and capabilities of external systems verified at the source, not assumed.

Hardware-verified fix: the label printer's advertised ZPL support was false and TSPL was required; the fix embodies establishing an external system's actual capability before integrating against its claims.

Frames a provider's stated behavior as an unverified claim - it may claim to be sending JSON but actually send plain text - prescribes treating responses as data until confirmed against expectations, and states that vendor-advertised hardening of client libraries cannot be trusted.
States the silent-failure consequence - a misrouted integration will appear to be working normally so you won't even know it's happening - and that a consistent error beats intermittent success.
